newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African chamber sees 1996 low for gold output.
newsitem.headline: S.African chamber sees 1996 low for gold output.

text.p: South Africa's gold mining industry is set for another substantial drop in output this year but 1996 should prove to be the trough, outgoing president of the Chamber of Mines At du Plessis said on Tuesday.
Speaking at the Chamber's 106th annual general meeting, he said there was likely to be a further "substantial reduction" in production in 1996 to around 500 tonnes.

Analysts told Reuters on Monday the industry was likely to produce under 490 tonnes of gold in 1996 after new figures showed production of 367.8 tonnes in the nine months to end-September compared to 390.5 in the same period last year.
Gold output dropped by 61.5 tonnes in 1995 to 522.4 tonnes -- the lowest level since 1956.
But du Plessis was confident the worst was now behind the industry.
"It is not anticipated -- at the level of 500 tonnes -- that there will be further significant reductions in South African gold delivery.
"With new developments scheduled to come on stream it is likely that gold production will remain at the 500-tonne mark for at least the foreseeable future," du Plessis said.

He added that the industry was developing several mega-ventures to expand existing shafts and sink new shafts which would yields "substantial" tonnages of gold and provide thousands of jobs well into the new century.
The South African mining industry's direct contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) declined in 1995 to 7.7 percent from 8.7 percent in 1994.
"This (decline) is attributed to the decline in gold production," du Plessis said.
But despite shrinking gold production, last year saw the value of total mineral sales rise to almost 57 billion rand -- assisted by a depreciation in the rand -- from 54 billion in 1994.

"The value of gold sales declined by more than six percent but the value of total sales was lifted by substantial increases in the sale of platinum group metals, chrome ore, copper, iron ore, nickel and coal," he said.
Total mineral exports in 1995 increased by more than three percent to 44 billion rand, almost 42 percent of South Africa's combined merchandise exports, du Plessis said.

"With sales valued at close to 13 billion rand, coal was the South African mining industry's second biggest earner (after gold) in 1995. This represented a 23 percent increase on 1994 sales," du Plessis said.
